title: Comparison of henselian local inertia with inertia in a global separable closure
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $\Omega$, namely the elements satisfying a monic polynomial over $A$, and choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ above $\mathfrak m$. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$, $D=\{g\in G:g\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q\}$ and $I=\{g\in D:g|_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}=1\}$. Let $A^{\mathrm h}$ and $A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be compatible henselization and strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with residue fields $\kappa$ and a chosen separable closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. There are compatible embeddings $A\subseteq A^{\mathrm h}\subseteq A^{\mathrm{sh}}\subseteq B_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\Omega$ realizing the residue choice. Both henselizations are domains. With $K^{\mathrm h}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm h})$ and $K^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(A^{\mathrm{sh}})$, one has
$$D=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm h}}(\Omega),\qquad I=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega).$$
The field $\Omega$ is a separable closure of $K^{\mathrm h}$. Under this identification the residue homomorphism is the continuous surjection
$$D\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)$$
with kernel $I$. In particular the inertia kernel of the henselian local field $K^{\mathrm h}$, defined as the kernel of its absolute Galois group acting on the separable residue closure, maps to precisely $I\subseteq G$. All the group identifications use their Krull topologies. For any chosen compatible embedding $K^{\mathrm{sh}}\subseteq\Omega$ as above, the same conclusion identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)$ with that local inertia kernel.

proof.text: Put $H=A^{\mathrm h}$, $R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$, $E=T/\mathfrak m_T$. Apply [lem-dl-a1-separable-normalization-local-embeddings]. It gives the normal domains, ind-etale structural maps, residue identification, and unique compatible local embeddings for each residue embedding $j$. Fix any such $j$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, and Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia; assembly of the six extracted obligations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-ind-etale-domain-generic-field] to $A\hookrightarrow H$ and $H\hookrightarrow R$. Their generic fibres are their fraction fields $K^{\mathrm h}$ and $K^{\mathrm{sh}}$, separable algebraic over $K$ and $K^{\mathrm h}$ respectively. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega$ is a separable closure over both intermediate fields.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, and Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia; assembly of the six extracted obligations.

proof.text: By [lem-dl-a1-henselian-normalization-localization], the integral closure $C$ of $H$ in $\Omega$ equals $T$, and $D=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm h}}(\Omega)$. Thus $D$ acts on $T$ over $H$. Apply [lem-dl-a1-ind-etale-residue-action-rigidity] with $\Gamma=D$: residue restriction defines $r$ and its kernel is exactly the automorphisms fixing $R$. Fixing a domain is equivalent to fixing its fractions; hence $\ker r=I=\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, and Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia; assembly of the six extracted obligations.

proof.text: By [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts], $R$ is also the strict henselization of $H$ with the same residue identification. Given $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)$, [lem-dl-a1-strict-henselization-residue-automorphism-lift] lifts it to an $H$-automorphism of $R$ and then to $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_{K^{\mathrm h}}(\Omega)=D$. By step 3, $u$ preserves $T$; since $u|_R=t$, reduction gives $j(r(u)(a))=j(\tau(a))$ for every residue element $a$. Injectivity of $j$ yields $r(u)=\tau$, proving surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, section-ramification, and Tag 0BSW, lemma-identify-inertia; assembly of the six extracted obligations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-residue-action-krull-continuity] to the two intermediate fraction fields and to the residue action of $D$ on $T$. This gives both claimed Krull-topology identifications and continuity of $r$. Because $C=T$, this residue action is the henselian local residue action, so its kernel maps to exactly $I\subseteq G$. The initial choice of $j$ was arbitrary, and uniqueness in [lem-dl-a1-separable-normalization-local-embeddings] covers every compatible embedding in the statement.
